full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 04.08.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Review Case No.04 of 2009 arising out of Writ Petition No.10371 of 2006. 

 2. Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary Ministry of Housing and Public Works (the present petitioner No.1) filed the said application for review of the judgment and order dated 24.03.2009. passed in Writ Petition No.10371 of 2006. It was asserted in the said review application that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 filed the Writ Petition. No.10371 of 2006 against the respondent Government, challenging the inaction of the respondents to implement their decision contained in Memo No.Shaklui-6/52-1/81/29 dated 12.01.1992, issued by the respondent No.3 to the predecessor of the petitioners and also seeking direction to the respondents to execute the lease deed in respect of bigha of, land of plot No.346 in Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka. Rule was issued in that writ petition and notice of the rule was served upon the respondents but none of the respondents entered appearance though the rule was made ready for hearing Thereafter on 12.08.2008 the rule appeared in the list of the Bench, presided over by his lordship Mr. Justice A. E M. Abdur Rahman. On 22,03.2009 the said rule was listed as item No.250 and on that day the learned Advocate for the petitioner prayed for upgrading the matter and the Court was pleased to upgrade the same and the said rule appeared in the list on 23.03.2009 as part heard. On that date adjournment was sought for on behalf of the Government on the ground of non-preparation for hearing, since the relevant file was not at the disposal of the concerned learned Deputy Attorney General. But the Hon'ble Court was pleased to ask the learned Deputy Attorney General for the respondent to make submission upon going through the record available before the Court and accordingly the learned Deputy Attorney General made verbal submission for the respondent which was not actually based on the actual case of the Government. Thereafter their Lordships, on conclusion of the hearing, fixed 24.03.2009 for passing judgment and on the said date their Lordships passed the impugned judgment and order making the rule absolute. But as some vital points have been discovered subsequent to the passing of the judgment after reviewing the Government's file in respect of the disputed land the respondents filed the review application on the ground of non-representation of actual facts of the case. 

 3. It was further asserted in that review application that the writ petitioner in a motivated manner withheld certain facts from the notice of Court and obtained the judgment. The review petitioner asserted also that through the letter dated 01.12.1985, annexure-D to the writ petition, the respondent cancelled the lease of the predecessor of the petitioner in respect of plot No.246 of Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka, but inadvertently it addressed to one Golam Rahman Mallik and Company instead of M/S. L. Mallik and Company. But subsequently another correct letter was issued in the name of M/S. L. Mallik and Company. That the petitioner suppressed the facts also that on 27.11.1994, he filed an application before the civil court to revive the Title Suit No.27 of 1991 which was filed by the predecessor of the writ petitioner challenging the order of cancellation of his lease and that application was ultimately rejected vide order No.43 dated 29.3.1995. Thereafter M/S. L. Mallik and Company filed another Title Suit being No.212 of 1995 in the court of the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for permanent injunction with a prayer for temporary injunction in respect of selfsame 1 bigha of land of plot No.246 of Tejgaon Industrial Area, but the prayer for temporary injunction was rejected by the order dated 29.10.1995. As against the said order the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.295 of 1995 which also was dismissed for default on 05.02.1997. Against this dismissal order the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.48 of 1998 which is still pending. That the petitioner suppressed the fact also that the disputed 1 bigha of land was leased out to others, that out the said 1 bigha, 10 kathas of land located at the West-north of the said plot was allotted to "Hanif Industries" through lease deed No.3788 dated 28.09.1987 and another 10 kathas of the said plot Was subsequently allotted to "Dainik Janakantha" on 16.02.1999 and the rest 4.3 kathas was kept reserved for entrance. That the possession of the said allotted land was duly handed over to the lessee upon receiving the lease money. In the review application  it was further asserted that the letter dated 12.01.1992 was issued in quite improper manner as on the very date of issuance of their letter there was no existence of the said 1 bigha of land. Because the very lease of M/S. L. Mallik and Company was cancelled through letter dated 01.12.1985  for flagrant violation of the condition of the said lease deed. That had the documents regarding the lease in favour of "Hanif  Industries" and "Dainik  Janakantha" been produced at the time of i hearing of the rule the impugned judgment and order would not have been passed and as such the said judgment is requited to be reviewed since the applicant could not produce those vital documents at the time of hearing the rule. The High Court Division upon hearing the learned Counsel for the review applicant and considering the facts and circumstances rejected the review application by, the impugned judgment and order on pointing out the facts that the notice of the rule was served upon the respondents long before in the year 2007 and the rule was made ready for hearing and also fixed for hearing before a Bench in the year 2008 and making also observations and comments thus: "As the rule was heard in presence of the learned Assistant Attorney General for the respondents State it was incumbent upon the respondent to bring all the facts in order to controvert the assertion made in the writ petition. But no affidavit-in-opposition was filed which clearly indicates that the writ respondents have no controversy with the assertions made by the writ petitioner. Therefore the question of error on the face of the record and discovery of any other evidence on important matter does not arise at all to have a review of the decision made by this Bench in Writ Petition No.10371 of 2006 on 24.03.2009." 

 i. For that the writ petition No. 10371 of 2006 having being heard and disposed of without giving effective opportunities of proper representation by the respondents in spite of the fact that the law officer who appeared in the case prayed for adjournment for filing affidavit-in-opposition and proper preparation of the case, the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the application for review.
